items.content: Below, the cities are scattered like broken necklaces, strings of amber and white light pooling in the darkness where human beings have gathered together against the cold. The plane hums its steady, indifferent note, suspended between one world and another. She pressed her forehead to the cold oval of the window and thought that from up here, all those burning rooms and lit streets looked almost like something beautiful — like grief, like longing, like everything people build when they are afraid of the dark.

items.content: The streets had shrunk somehow, or perhaps she had grown in ways that had nothing to do with height. She walked past the bakery, the hardware store, the particular bend in the road where she had once crashed her bicycle, and felt the strange doubling of memory laid over reality like tracing paper. Everything was familiar and foreign at once — a language she had once spoken fluently but now stumbled through, searching for words that no longer quite fit her mouth.

items.content: The last light came slowly, the way it always does in autumn — not fading so much as retreating, pulling itself up the sides of buildings like a tide going out. The upper floors of the old offices caught it first, their windows suddenly molten, briefly alive with something that looked almost like fire. Down in the street, the shadows had already claimed everything, cool and certain, while above them the rooftops held on a little longer, glowing for no one in particular.
